cells.tense: You are holding the line right now, with nothing to show for it yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are holding steady and do one small practical piece of it today, whether or not you feel like it.
cells.core:
You are carrying this one through, and you are still at it. No clear road shows ahead, only the next stretch, and you take it anyway. That is not a mood passing through. It is something you keep choosing while the outcome stays open.

What makes it worth keeping is that you do not wait for the whole shape to arrive. You do a small piece with your own hands, let it stand, and go on. Keep feeding it the same way — one honest stretch at a time, no need to know where it ends. Strength shows up because you spend it, not because you save it for a day that clears.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the line moving without seeing the whole road.
cells.verb: holding to the course through a drawn-out practical strain
cells.place: in the low light of a road you can see one bend ahead of

cells.tense: You will outlast this if you have to, and you are already bracing to prove it.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are holding that someone else could carry or share, and hand it over today without correcting how they do it.
cells.core:
The readiness to endure has gone past the moment. You are gripping everything ahead of time — planning for pressure that has not landed, rehearsing stamina that may not be called on. It stops being patience when it turns into a guard post you stay in.

What you are strong enough for is to not pick up every weight the second it appears. Some of it belongs in other hands, and taking it all quietly is a show of force. Let one load be someone else's for an afternoon. The ground under you is firmer when your feet are not planted across every road ahead.

cells.tense: You stopped holding this a while back, and you still stand where you gave up.
cells.ask: Choose one small promise to yourself, keep it today, and let it be finished without making it mean anything larger.
cells.core:
There is a steadiness you had and it has gone quiet. Something practical got heavy, the weight went down, and the hand has not gone back to it. The strength did not vanish. The grip did.

One small thing that holds, finished today, is what this looks like when it is working. Start with something you can close out — not the whole problem, just a knot you can tie. Let that be enough on its own, without it standing for anything bigger. Steadiness grows back the way it left: quietly, through the next small thing you actually do.

cells.tense: You are already holding steady through this, and you call it just getting through the day.
cells.ask: Say out loud one thing you have kept going through, and count it as yours, not as fate or chance.
cells.core:
Look at what you have been carrying without calling it strength. You wake up, do the small hard things, and keep pushing through a situation with no clean answer — and you describe it as something happening around you, not something you are doing. The pushing is real, and it belongs to you.

Said plainly, when this is running well it sounds like: this one was mine, I moved it. Not a mood passing through, not something that landed on you. A person pushing a hard thing forward, one stretch at a time, and taking the credit for it. Claim one piece, even privately, and let the credit sit where it belongs.
cells.sheetLine: The steady pushing is running. You just haven't claimed it.
